hints: Look closely at the large dark oval organelles with stacked membranes inside, what pigment-containing organelle is unique to photosynthetic cells?
Remember which structures are found in both plant and animal cells (nucleus, mitochondria, cell membrane) and which are found only in plant cells.
walkthrough:
**Observe the key structures in the image**

Look at the cell in the photomicrograph. You can see several large, dark organelles with internal stacks of membranes. These are chloroplasts with grana and thylakoids. You can also see a very large central vacuole and a cell wall at the edge.

**Apply the plant versus animal rule**

Here is the simple rule to remember. Some organelles are shared: both plant and animal cells have a nucleus, mitochondria and a cell membrane. Only plant cells have chloroplasts, a large permanent vacuole and a cellulose cell wall.

**Choose the statement with correct logic**

The cell must be a plant cell, but the reason given must also be correct. Chloroplasts are only found in plant cells, so that alone proves it. A nucleus, mitochondria or cell membrane cannot prove it because animal cells have them too.

options.A: The cell is a plant cell, but the reasoning is wrong. Both plant and animal cells have a nucleus, so a nucleus cannot prove it is a plant cell.
options.B: Correct and well done. Chloroplasts are found only in plant cells for photosynthesis, so their presence proves this is a plant cell.
options.C: Not correct. Both plant and animal cells have a cell membrane, so this cannot be used to identify it as an animal cell.
options.D: Not correct. Both plant and animal cells have mitochondria for aerobic respiration, so this cannot prove it is an animal cell.
